diff_summary.old_string:
"""Implementations of the Bench CLI commands (verify, ledger, stats,
constitution, viewer).

Each command returns an int exit code (0 on success, 1 on failure) and
prints a human-readable summary to stdout. Error diagnostics go to stderr
so the two streams can be separated in scripts.

These commands are read-only reports over the ledger and constitution —
nothing here mutates state, so there is no risk of collision with the
governance pipeline running in parallel.
"""
diff_summary.new_string:
"""Implementations of the Bench CLI commands (verify, ledger, stats,
constitution, viewer, retire, audit-retirement).

Each command returns an int exit code (0 on success, 1 on failure) and
prints a human-readable summary to stdout. Error diagnostics go to stderr
so the two streams can be separated in scripts.

All but one of these are read-only reports over the ledger and constitution,
so there is no risk of collision with the governance pipeline running in
parallel. The exception is ``cmd_retire``, which archives the active chain and
opens a successor under C-008's single bounded exception to ledger
immutability. It holds no logic of its own: every decision, guard, and write
lives in ``ledger/retire.py``, and this module only parses arguments, supplies
the real ``sys.stdin.isatty`` and ``input``, and renders the result.
"""

findings.evidence: "The exception is ``cmd_retire``, which archives the active chain and opens a successor under C-008's single bounded exception to ledger immutability... every decision, guard, and write lives in ``ledger/retire.py``"
findings.reasoning: This diff only edits a docstring in cli/commands.py and asserts that cmd_retire correctly implements C-008's bounded retirement exception, but the actual retirement logic (human-decision gating, pre-move verify_chain check, anchor entry contents, archive path recording) lives in ledger/retire.py, which is not part of this diff. The claim of compliance cannot be verified from what's shown here; the substantive C-008 review needs to happen against ledger/retire.py itself, not this comment describing it.

findings.evidence: "(verify, ledger, stats, constitution, viewer, retire, audit-retirement)"
findings.reasoning: The docstring documents two new commands (retire, audit-retirement) as if their implementations already exist in this file, but no corresponding cmd_retire/cmd_audit_retirement function bodies appear in the diff. This is consistent with the change being a doc-only update landing alongside a separate implementation change, but if this is the entirety of the intended change set, the doc claims outpace the visible code and the pipeline should confirm the implementing diff(s) are reviewed under the same governance run.

rebuttals.argument: The Challenger is asking this diff to prove something it explicitly disclaims responsibility for. The new docstring's own language is the key evidence: it says cmd_retire 'holds no logic of its own: every decision, guard, and write lives in ledger/retire.py, and this module only parses arguments, supplies the real sys.stdin.isatty and input, and renders the result.' That is not a claim of C-008 compliance being made by this file; it is an accurate architectural statement disclaiming that this file is where compliance should be checked. A docstring in cli/commands.py cannot itself violate C-008 because C-008 governs code that writes to, moves, or archives ledger entries, and this diff contains zero lines that touch the ledger, chain hashes, or file I/O. The Challenger's finding is correctly scoped as an OBSERVATION rather than a violation, and I'd go further: it isn't even a live risk on this diff, because there's nothing here for C-008 to attach to. The correct place to run the substantive C-008 audit is whatever diff introduces ledger/retire.py, not this one.
rebuttals.evidence: New docstring text: 'It holds no logic of its own: every decision, guard, and write lives in ``ledger/retire.py``, and this module only parses arguments, supplies the real ``sys.stdin.isatty`` and ``input``, and renders the result.' The diff's old_string/new_string pair shows only docstring prose changed; no function bodies, imports, or ledger calls are present.

rebuttals.argument: The Challenger is right that cmd_retire and cmd_audit_retirement don't appear as function bodies in this diff, and that's worth flagging procedurally. But this alone doesn't establish a C-002 scope violation on the evidence shown. CLAUDE.md's own Project Structure listing already shows commands.py as the home for CLI commands generally ('verify, ledger, stats, constitution, viewer'), and per rule 14 ('One change per tool call'), it's normal and expected for a governed edit that adds retire/audit-retirement to land as multiple discrete Edit/Write calls, each independently governed: one adding the docstring, others adding the actual function implementations. A module docstring documenting the file's full command surface, including commands implemented via other calls in the same session, is standard practice, not scope creep. The finding is appropriately hedged by the Challenger itself ('if this is the entirety of the intended change set') and doesn't assert a definitive violation. I'd concede the underlying caution is reasonable pipeline hygiene, i.e., the Oracle or a human auditor should confirm the implementing diffs for cmd_retire/cmd_audit_retirement were separately governed, but that is a process check outside the four corners of this diff, not a defect in this diff.
rebuttals.evidence: CLAUDE.md rule 14: 'One change per tool call. Do not batch unrelated changes into a single Write/Edit operation.' New docstring only adds prose naming 'retire, audit-retirement' alongside existing commands; no new function definitions appear in old_string/new_string.

defender.summary: This is a narrow, accurate docstring-only edit that makes no ledger writes and explicitly defers all C-008-relevant logic to ledger/retire.py, so neither finding identifies an actual defect in the diff shown, though the Oracle should confirm the referenced retire/audit-retirement implementations are or will be governed under their own pipeline runs.

oracle.reasoning: This diff modifies only the module docstring in cli/commands.py. The old_string/new_string pair shows exclusively prose changes: it renames the command surface to include 'retire, audit-retirement' and adds an architectural note that cmd_retire defers all C-008-relevant logic to ledger/retire.py. No function bodies, imports, ledger writes, hash-chain operations, or file I/O appear in the diff. Both Challenger findings are explicitly graded as OBSERVATIONS, not violations, and the Defender's rebuttals are sound. On finding 0 (C-008): the Defender correctly argues that C-008 governs code that writes to, moves, or archives ledger entries, and this diff contains zero such lines. A docstring describing where compliance lives cannot itself violate ledger immutability; the substantive C-008 audit belongs to whatever diff introduces ledger/retire.py. I concur. On finding 1 (C-002): the docstring documents the file's full command surface, which is coherent, single-scope work. Per CLAUDE.md rule 14 ('One change per tool call'), it is expected that the implementing function bodies land as separate governed edits. Documenting the intended command surface alongside existing commands (verify, ledger, stats, constitution, viewer) is standard practice and does not bundle unrelated edits. The change stays within one coherent scope as required by C-002. I checked the remaining constraints independently: C-001 (no catch blocks touched), C-003 (no imports added), C-004 (no type annotations changed), C-006 (no secrets), C-007 (cli/commands.py is not in pipeline/, ledger/, or hooks/, and nothing here weakens enforcement or logging) are all satisfied or not applicable. The one procedural caveat, shared by both Challenger and Defender, is that the referenced cmd_retire/cmd_audit_retirement implementations and ledger/retire.py must be governed under their own pipeline runs; that is a process check outside the four corners of this diff, not a defect in it.

constraint_citations.note: No error-handling or catch blocks appear in this docstring-only change.

cli/commands.py is not a pipeline/ledger/hooks file; the docstring adds no logic that weakens enforcement, bypasses verification, or disables logging.

The diff contains no ledger writes, moves, archives, or hash-chain operations. The docstring only describes that cmd_retire defers such logic to ledger/retire.py. C-008 has nothing to attach to here; the substantive audit belongs to the diff introducing ledger/retire.py, as both Challenger (finding 0) and Defender agree.

advisories: The implementing logic for cmd_retire and cmd_audit_retirement, and ledger/retire.py, must each be reviewed under their own governance runs. C-008's bounded retirement exception requires (a) recorded explicit human decision, (b) an archived copy passing verify_chain with valid=true before the original is moved, (c) a fully populated anchor entry, and (d) indefinite archive retention. This docstring asserts that guarantee but does not contain the code that must satisfy it; the assertion should not be treated as evidence of compliance for the retirement implementation itself.

If this docstring is the entirety of the intended change set (i.e., the retire/audit-retirement implementations never land or land ungoverned), the documentation would overstate the file's actual command surface. A human auditor should confirm the implementing diffs were separately governed.
